issues.legal_issue: A repealed municipal tax rule is preserved only to the extent that its valuation basis is consistent with the replacement law.
material_facts: The replacement law required a statutory allowance to be deducted from gross annual letting value when assessing house tax.
The municipality continued to assess and collect tax using the earlier rule, which applied the tax to gross annual letting value without that deduction.
issues.conclusion: The earlier tax rule was not preserved insofar as it permitted assessment on gross annual letting value without the required deduction; the tax had to be assessed on the value after that deduction.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(c), 69 and 73(2) of the Madhya Bharat Municipalities Act, 1954, rules and taxes under a repealed enactment are deemed to continue only insofar as they are consistent with the new Act. Section 73(2) requires the statutory allowance to be deducted from annual letting value, so the earlier gross-value basis cannot be saved to the extent it conflicts with that requirement. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.municipal_tax_assessment: A municipal authority assesses a tax on buildings or land.
predicates.replacement_law_requires_allowance: The law governing the assessment requires an allowance to be deducted from the valuation used to assess the tax.
predicates.earlier_tax_basis_omits_allowance: The authority continues to use an earlier tax basis that does not deduct the required allowance.

issues.definition: When a municipal tax assessment is governed by a replacement law that requires an allowance, and the earlier tax basis omits it, the tax must use the value after the required allowance.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier municipal assessment list may be adopted for a later year, but it is subject to the procedure for publication, objections and authentication before becoming conclusive for that year.
material_facts: The municipality adopted an assessment list prepared for an earlier year for later official years.
The governing law permitted adoption of an earlier list, but required the provisions for publication and objections to apply to an adopted list as if it were a new list for that year.
The statute made an authenticated assessment list conclusive evidence of valuation and tax for the official year in which it was in force.
issues.conclusion: The municipality could adopt the earlier assessment list, but the adopted list became the assessment list for each later year subject to the applicable publication, objection and authentication procedures; it became conclusive for that year only after those procedures were followed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 75, 76 and 79(1)–(2) of the Madhya Bharat Municipalities Act, 1954 permit adoption of an earlier assessment list, subject to the process for publication, lodging and disposal of objections, and authentication. Under section 76(6), the list is conclusive for the relevant official year once authenticated, subject to the statutory qualifications. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

rule.if: municipal_tax_assessment and earlier_list_adopted_for_later_year and adopted_list_published and objection_process_completed and adopted_list_authenticated

predicates.municipal_tax_assessment: A municipal authority prepares or applies an assessment list for a municipal tax.
predicates.earlier_list_adopted_for_later_year: The authority adopts a list prepared for an earlier year for a later official year.
predicates.adopted_list_published: The adopted list is published for the later official year.
predicates.objection_process_completed: An opportunity to object to the adopted list is given and any objections are dealt with.
predicates.adopted_list_authenticated: The adopted list is formally authenticated after the objection process.

issues.definition: When a municipality adopts an earlier list for a later year and publishes, processes objections to, and authenticates it, the adopted list is conclusive for that year.
